verses.zh: 挪亚的儿子闪、含、雅弗的后代记在下面。洪水以后，他们都生了儿子。
verses.en: This is the account[NOTE:1] of Noah’s sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.[NOTE:2] Sons[NOTE:3] were born[NOTE:4] to them after the flood.
notes: The title אֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדֹת (ʾelleh toledot, here translated as “This is the account”) here covers 10:1-11:9, which contains the so-called Table of Nations and the account of how the nations came to be dispersed.
The sons are not listed in order by age. Japheth was oldest (10:21); Ham was youngest (9:24). Shem is listed first due to importance.

Sons were born to them. A vertical genealogy such as this encompasses more than the names of sons. The list includes cities, tribes, and even nations. In a loose way, the names in the list have some derivation or connection to the three ancestors.

It appears that the Table of Nations is a composite of at least two ancient sources: Some sections begin with the phrase “the sons of” (בְּנֵי, bene) while other sections use “begot” (יָלָד, yalad). It may very well be that the “sons of” list was an old, “bare bones” list that was retained in the family records, while the “begot” sections were editorial inserts by the writer of Genesis, reflecting his special interests. See A. P. Ross, “The Table of Nations in Genesis 10—Its Structure,” BSac 137 (1980): 340-53; idem, “The Table of Nations in Genesis 10—Its Content,” BSac 138 (1981): 22-34.
verses.commentary:
10:1 "Now these are the records of the generations" This phase is repeated three times in the
context of Genesis 10 and 11 (Gen. 10:1; 11:10,27). This was the author's way to outline the book or a
Babylonian colophon to mark the cuneiform clay tablets that go together. See full note at Gen. 2:4.

▣ "Shem, Ham, and Japheth" This order of listing their names is not primarily related to
their age but a theological arrangement, listing those in the Messianic line first, and those farthest
removed last. See the same list in 1 Chronicles 1.

verses.zh: 雅弗的儿子是歌篾、玛各、玛代、雅完、土巴、米设、提拉。
verses.en: The sons of Japheth[NOTE:1] were Gomer,[NOTE:2] Magog,[NOTE:3] Madai,[NOTE:4] Javan,[NOTE:5] Tubal,[NOTE:6] Meshech,[NOTE:7] and Tiras.[NOTE:8]
notes: The Greek form of the name Japheth, Iapetos, is used in Greek tradition for the ancestor of the Greeks.
Gomer was the ancestor of the Cimmerians. For a discussion of the Cimmerians see E. M. Yamauchi, Foes from the Northern Frontier (SBA), 49-61.
For a discussion of various proposals concerning the descendants of Magog see E. M. Yamauchi, Foes from the Northern Frontier (SBA), 22-24.
Madai was the ancestor of the Medes, who lived east of Assyria.
Javan was the father of the Hellenic race, the Ionians who lived in western Asia Minor.
Tubal was the ancestor of militaristic tribes that lived north of the Black Sea. For a discussion of ancient references to Tubal see E. M. Yamauchi, Foes from the Northern Frontier (SBA), 24-26.
Meshech was the ancestor of the people known in Assyrian records as the Musku. For a discussion of ancient references to them see E. M. Yamauchi, Foes from the Northern Frontier (SBA), 24-26.
Tiras was the ancestor of the Thracians, some of whom possibly became the Pelasgian pirates of the Aegean.
verses.commentary:
10:2 "Gomer" This seems to refer to the Cimmerians (BDB 170, KB 198), who are mentioned in Homer's Odyssey 11.13. They
inhabited northern Asia Minor. They possibly migrated north and became European tribal groups. This can be seen
through a similar term for them in north Germany, "Cimbi" and in Wales, "Cymri."

▣ "Magog" There has been much discussion about this name because of its connection to Ezekiel 38-39
and end-time events. However, it must be asserted that Magog (BDB 156, KB 544), along with Meshech and Tubal, also mentioned
in Gen. 10:2, are primarily tribes connected with Asia Minor and the coast of the Black Sea. It is quite
possible that they migrated north and became the tribal groups of modern Russia. But, in ancient times, they
were much closer to the Promised Land. Most assert that Magog is connected with the Scythians, southeast of
the Black Sea. This information comes from Josephus (Antiq. 1.12.3).

▣ "Madai" Most assert that this refers to the Medes (BDB 552, KB 548; see Edwin Yamauchi, The Stones and
The Scriptures, p. 43), who lived south and southwest of the Caspian Sea, who become so important to Israel in
their joining with Persia to overthrow the Neo-Babylon Empire (Nebuchadnezzar).

▣ "Javan" This (BDB 402, KB 402) seems to refer to the Ionian (southern) Greeks (cf. Dan. 8:21; 10:20; 11:2). This
group is spelled

- "Javana" in Sanskrit

- "Juna" in old Persian

- "Jounan" on the Rosetta stone

They later became, not only the kingdom of Greece, but possibly a part of the sea peoples in
the Aegean area (i.e., Phoenicians and Philistines).

▣ "Tubal" Many assert that this (BDB 1063, KB 1683) refers to the Tiberenians of central Asia Minor. Both Tubal and
Meshech occur in Ezekiel 38-39 as residing in Asia Minor.

▣ "Meshech" Many assert that this is a tribal group (BDB 604, KB 646 II) who lived south and southwest of the Black
Sea (cf. Ezek. 27:13; 32:26; 38:2; 39:1). This information comes from Herodotus (1.14).

The UBS Text Project, p. 17, changes the vowels to "Mosheth," and gives the change an "A" rating. LXX has
"Mosoch." Most English translations have "Meshech."

▣ "Tiras" There have been several possible identifications for this group (BDB 1066, KB 1728) because this name,
nor any of his descendants, are listed. Many of these names and locales are simply uncertain. The possibilities include

- the Etruscans

- an Aegean pirate nation called Pelasgians

- Josephus says the Thracians

- Rashi says that it refers to Persia

verses.zh: 歌篾的儿子是亚实基拿、利法、陀迦玛。
verses.en: The sons of Gomer were[NOTE:1] Ashkenaz,[NOTE:2] Riphath,[NOTE:3] and Togarmah.[NOTE:4]
notes: The descendants of Gomer were all northern tribes of the Upper Euphrates.
Ashkenaz was the ancestor of a northern branch of Indo-Germanic tribes, possibly Scythians. For discussion see E. M. Yamauchi, Foes from the Northern Frontier (SBA), 63.
The descendants of Riphath lived in a district north of the road from Haran to Carchemish.

Togarmah is also mentioned in Ezek 38:6, where it refers to Til-garimmu, the capital of Kammanu, which bordered Tabal in eastern Turkey. See E. M. Yamauchi, Foes from the Northern Frontier (SBA), 26, n. 28.
verses.commentary:
10:3 "Ashkenaz" This is the name (BDB 79, KB 95) adopted later by Jews of Europe (i.e., Germany). The current theories are

- Scythians in the area of Germany (Herodotus calls them Scythians)

- people close to Lake Urumia

- a tribal group of Bithynia in Asia Minor

▣ "Riphath" 1 Chronicles 1:6 has "Dipthah" but the LXX and Vulgate have the "R" ("R" ‒ "D" confusion in
Hebrew texts; see note at "Dodanim" below). This has been alleged to be a tribal group (BDB 937, KB 1227) near the river
Rhebas or a tribal group near the Bosphorus. Josephus (Antiq. 1.6.1) puts them in Asia Minor.

▣ "Togarmah" These (BDB 1062 KB 1688) are

- a tribal group in the area of Cappadocia in Asia Minor

- near the ancient city of Carchemish

- a tribal group in Phrygia

All three of these possibilities are in modern Turkey.

verses.zh: 雅完的儿子是以利沙、他施、基提、多单。
verses.en: The sons of Javan were Elishah,[NOTE:1] Tarshish,[NOTE:2] the Kittim,[NOTE:3] and the Dodanim.[NOTE:4]
notes: The descendants of Elishah populated Cyprus.
The descendants of Tarshish settled along the southern coast of what is modern Turkey. However, some identify the site Tarshish (see Jonah 1:3) with Sardinia or Spain.
The name Kittim is associated with Cyprus, as well as coastlands east of Rhodes. It is used in later texts to refer to the Romans.

Most of the MT mss read “Dodanim” here, but 1 Chr 1:7 has “Rodanim,” perhaps referring to the island of Rhodes. But the Qere reading in 1 Chr 1:7 suggests “Dodanim.” Dodona is one of the most ancient and revered spots in ancient Greece.
verses.commentary:
10:4 "Elishah" Most assert that this refers (BDB 47, KB 56) to the native population of Cypress. They are mentioned in Ezek. 27:7.

▣ "Tarshish" Although Albright located this at Sardinia, most modern researchers locate it in southern
Spain (i.e., Tartessos). It is mentioned in 2 Chr. 9:21; Ps. 48:7; 72:10; Jonah 1:3; 4:2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TARSHISH

▣ "Kittim" There is a consistent opinion that this refers to the settlers on the east coast of Cypress
(BDB 508, KB 504; 1 Chr. 1:7). Josephus (Antiq. 1.6.1) relates it to the Cyprian city of "Kition" on the south
central coast of Cypress (i.e., Num. 24:24; Isa. 23:1; Ezek. 27:6).

▣ "Dodanim" Notice the name ending in "im," which is the Hebrew PLURAL that may
denote a family or tribe. Many assert that the similarity between the Hebrew letters, D (ד) and
R (ר), has been confused and that this refers to the tribal inhabitants of the Island of Rhodes
(BDB 922, cf. 1 Chr. 1:7; see NEB, LXX, and NIV translations, as well as the UBS Text Project, p. 16, gives
"Rodanites" an "A" rating). However, others assert that it is northern Greece and still others say it is
southern Italy. It is obvious that this is simply unknown (BDB 187, KB 214).

verses.zh: 这些人的后裔将各国的地土、海岛分开居住，各随各的方言、宗族立国。
verses.en: From these the coastlands of the nations were separated into their lands, every one according to its language, according to their families, by their nations.
verses.commentary:
10:5 "From these the coastlands of the nations" This phrase is used metaphorically for far away
peoples, but here it seems to refer to the inhabitants along the coast of the Mediterranean and Black Seas
which follows the migration of the children of Japheth.

▣ "their lands. . .his language. . .their families. . .their nations" This seems to be a
fourfold division of how this chapter is divided:

- geographically

- linguistically

- ethnically

- politically

verses.zh: 含的儿子是古实、麦西、弗、迦南。
verses.en: The sons of Ham were Cush,[NOTE:1] Mizraim,[NOTE:2] Put,[NOTE:3] and Canaan.[NOTE:4]
notes: The descendants of Cush settled in Nubia (Ethiopia).
The descendants of Mizraim settled in Upper and Lower Egypt.
The descendants of Put settled in Libya.
The descendants of Canaan lived in the region of Phoenicia (Palestine).
verses.commentary:
10:6 "Cush and Mizraim and Put and Canaan" These sons of Ham are discussed further in the following verses:

- Cush (Nubia, BDB 468, KB 466) in Gen. 10:7-12

- Mizraim (Egypt, BDB 595, KB 625) in Gen. 10:13-14

- Canaan (BDB 488) in Gen. 10:15-19

- Put (BDB 806, KB 917), although not discussed, seems to refer either to East Africa (Somalia), southern Arabia, Libya or Cyrene

It is obvious from this many possible locations that we are uncertain.

verses.zh: 古实的儿子是西巴、哈腓拉、撒弗他、拉玛、撒弗提迦。拉玛的儿子是示巴、底但。
verses.en: The sons of Cush were Seba,[NOTE:1] Havilah,[NOTE:2] Sabtah,[NOTE:3] Raamah,[NOTE:4] and Sabteca.[NOTE:5] The sons of Raamah were Sheba[NOTE:6] and Dedan.[NOTE:7]
notes: The descendants of Seba settled in Upper Egypt along the Nile.
The Hebrew name Havilah apparently means “stretch of sand” (see HALOT 297 s.v. חֲוִילָה). Havilah’s descendants settled in eastern Arabia.
The descendants of Sabtah settled near the western shore of the Persian Gulf in ancient Hadhramaut.
The descendants of Raamah settled in southwest Arabia.
The descendants of Sabteca settled in Samudake, east toward the Persian Gulf.
Sheba became the name of a kingdom in southwest Arabia.
The name Dedan is associated with ʿUla in northern Arabia.
verses.commentary:
10:7 "Seba" This is the area of the upper Nile as far as we can tell from the information that is
now available (BDB 685, KB 738). It is mentioned in Isa. 43:3.

▣ "Havilah" This is literally "sandland" (BDB 296, KB 297), possibly located somewhere in Egypt.

▣ "Sabtah" This (BDB 688, KB 741) can either be in the area of modern Ethiopia, which would be east
Africa, or a city in Arabia.

▣ "Raamah" This seems to be the Sabateans of southwest Arabia (BDB 947, KB 1268 III).

▣ "Sabteca" This also refers to Ethiopia (BDB 688, KB 741).

▣ "Sheba" This (BDB 985, KB 1381, #2) seems to be the famous area of the Queen of Sheba, southwest of Arabia
(cf. 1 Kgs. 10:1-10; Job 1:15; 6:19; Ps. 72:10,15; Isa. 60:6; Jer. 6:20).

▣ "Dedan" This seems to be somewhere in Arabia (BDB 186, KB 214). It is obvious that the sons of Cush
are located in east Africa and the Arabian peninsula. It is mentioned in Isa. 21:13; Jer. 25:23; 49:8;
Ezek. 25:13; 27:20.

verses.zh: 古实又生宁录，他为世上英雄之首。
verses.en: Cush was the father of[NOTE:1] Nimrod; he began to be a valiant warrior on the earth.
notes: Heb “fathered.” Embedded within Cush’s genealogy is an account of Nimrod, a mighty warrior. There have been many attempts to identify him, but none are convincing.
verses.commentary:
10:8 "father of Nimrod" Nimrod (BDB 650, KB 701) is particularly named because he was a founder of the
first major civilization. This would mean that descendants of Ham developed Babylon. He is linked with
the sons of Cush (cf. 1 Chr. 1:10) because of the linguistic similarities to the name Kassites. There are
two groups from Cush, one in Gen. 10:7 on the eastern side of the Red Sea and this one in Gen. 10:8 on
the western side of the Red Sea.

▣ "Nimrod" The term seems to mean "revolt" according to Rashi and Leupold. With this in mind
the next two major phrases, "mighty one" and "mighty hunter," are interpreted negatively as "tyrant" or
"conqueror" or "killer of men." However, we are uncertain if this is the connotation, but it seems to fit
the context. This man is going to build some of the major cities of Mesopotamia (see list in v. 10 and
another in v. 11) and he will apparently start the first world power. Many have asserted that this refers
to Tukuli-ninurta I, but he did not live until the thirteenth century B.C. when he
controlled Assyria and Babylon. He was called Ninus, but his time is much too late to fit that of
Nimrod. Others assert that this refers to Sargon I, ruler of the city of Akkad.

verses.zh: 他在耶和华面前是个英勇的猎户，所以俗语说：「像宁录在耶和华面前是个英勇的猎户。」
verses.en: He was a mighty hunter[NOTE:1] before the Lord.[NOTE:2] (That is why it is said, “Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the Lord.”)
notes: The Hebrew word for “hunt” is צַיִד (tsayid), which is used on occasion for hunting men (1 Sam 24:12; Jer 16:16; Lam 3:15).

Another option is to take the divine name here, לִפְנֵי יִהוָה (lifne yehvah, “before the Lord [YHWH]”), as a means of expressing the superlative degree. In this case one may translate “Nimrod was the greatest hunter in the world.”
verses.commentary:
10:9 "a mighty hunter before the Lord" Some commentators assert that
God taking notice of a hunter is beneath His dignity, but if the phrase refers to the first conqueror
and developer of a human world system (cf. Mic. 5:6), then God taking notice of him is understandable.

verses.zh: 他国的起头是巴别、以力、亚甲、甲尼，都在示拿地。
verses.en: The primary regions[NOTE:1] of his kingdom were Babel,[NOTE:2] Erech,[NOTE:3] Akkad,[NOTE:4] and Calneh[NOTE:5] in the land of Shinar.[NOTE:6]
notes: Heb “beginning.” E. A. Speiser, Genesis (AB), 67, suggests “mainstays,” citing Jer 49:35 as another text where the Hebrew noun is so used.
Or “Babylon.”
Erech (ancient Uruk, modern Warka), one of the most ancient civilizations, was located southeast of Babylon.
Akkad, or ancient Agade, was associated with Sargon and located north of Babylon.
No such place is known in Shinar (i.e., Babylonia). Therefore some have translated the Hebrew term כַלְנֵה (khalneh) as “all of them,” referring to the three previous names (cf. NRSV).
Shinar is another name for Babylonia.
verses.commentary:
10:10 All of the cities listed in this verse were major cities in Shinar (southern Tigris and Euphrates
River valley) at one time of another.

▣ "Babel" The Babylonians say that the name of the city (bab-ili) means "the gate of the
gods," which refers to its large ziggurat. However, in Genesis 11, the Jews interpreted it as meaning
(balil), "he confused" (BDB 93, KB 107).

▣ "Erech" R. K. Harrison, Old Testament Times, pp. 38-39, thinks this name (BDB 74,
KB 88 II) refers to the ancient city of Uruk, which is dates from the end of the fourth millennium B.C.
(Chalcolithic Period: Uruk Phase). It also had a ziggurat in its center.

▣ "Calneh" Some say that this (BDB 484, KB 480) refers to a city of Nippur, while others re-verbalize
this to mean "all of them." The UBS Text Project, p. 17, agrees with this and gives it a "B" rating (some
doubt). See the NEB and RSV translations.

▣ "the land of Shinar" This is linguistically related to the term "Sumer" or "Sumeria" (BDB 1042 KB 1607).
It refers to an area of southern Mesopotamia, the first known civilization that developed writing
(6,000 ‒ 4,000 B.C.).

verses.zh: 他从那地出来往亚述去，建造尼尼微、利河伯、迦拉，
verses.en: From that land he went[NOTE:1] to Assyria,[NOTE:2] where he built Nineveh,[NOTE:3] Rehoboth Ir,[NOTE:4] Calah,[NOTE:5]
notes: The subject of the verb translated “went” is probably still Nimrod. However, it has also been interpreted that “Ashur went,” referring to a derivative power.
Heb “Asshur.”
Nineveh was an ancient Assyrian city situated on the Tigris River.
The name Rehoboth Ir means “and broad streets of a city,” perhaps referring to a suburb of Nineveh.
Calah (modern Nimrud) was located 20 miles north of Nineveh.
verses.commentary:
10:11 "he went forth into Assyria" Some say that this refers to Nimrod and that seems to fit the
context best (cf. Mic. 5:6). However, others, including the Septuagint, the Vulgate, the Syriac, Martin
Luther, and John Calvin, say it refers to Asshur.

▣ "Nineveh" This (BDB 644, KB 696) is the major capital of the Assyrian Empire located on the Tigris
River (cf. 2 Kgs. 19:36; Isa. 37:37; Jonah 1:2; 3:2-7; 4:11; Nah. 1:1; 2:8; 3:7; Zeph. 2:13).

▣ "Rehoboth-Ir" This name (BDB 932) literally means "wide street city" or "wide places of the city" and probably
is a description of Nineveh (BDB 944 II).

▣ "Calah" This is a major Assyrian city (BDB 480 II, KB 478 II). Its modern name is Nimrud which is obviously
connected to the name, Nimrod.

verses.zh: 和尼尼微、迦拉中间的利鲜，这就是那大城。
verses.en: and Resen, which is between Nineveh and the great city Calah.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and Resen between Nineveh and Calah; it [i.e., Calah] is the great city.”

verses.zh: 麦西生路低人、亚拿米人、利哈比人、拿弗土希人、
verses.en: Mizraim[NOTE:1] was the father of[NOTE:2] the Ludites,[NOTE:3] Anamites,[NOTE:4] Lehabites,[NOTE:5] Naphtuhites,[NOTE:6]
notes: Mizraim is the Hebrew name for Egypt (cf. NRSV).
Heb “fathered.”
The Ludites were African tribes west of the Nile Delta.
The Anamites lived in North Africa, west of Egypt, near Cyrene.
The Lehabites are identified with the Libyans.
The Naphtuhites lived in Lower Egypt (the Nile Delta region).
verses.commentary:
10:13 "Mizraim" Many assert this refers to upper and lower Egypt (BDB 595).

▣ "Ludim" This may refer to Lydians in Asia Minor (BDB 530, KB 521).

▣ "Anamim" This may be a tribal group occupying the oasis west of Egypt (BDB 777, KB 857).

▣ "Lehabim" This seems to refer to the desert tribes of the northern African coast (BDB 529, KB 520).

▣ "Naphtuhim" This seems to be the tribal group near the city of Memphis (BDB 661, KB 714). All of those
mentioned in Gen. 10:13 are obviously connected with Egypt and the surrounding area.

verses.zh: 帕斯鲁细人、迦斯路希人、迦斐托人；从迦斐托出来的有非利士人。
verses.en: Pathrusites,[NOTE:1] Casluhites[NOTE:2] (from whom the Philistines came),[NOTE:3] and Caphtorites.[NOTE:4]
notes: The Pathrusites are known in Egyptian as P-to-reshi; they resided in Upper Egypt.
The Casluhites lived in Crete and eventually settled east of the Egyptian Delta, between Egypt and Canaan.

Several commentators prefer to reverse the order of the words to put this clause after the next word, since the Philistines came from Crete (where the Caphtorites lived). But the table may suggest migration rather than lineage, and the Philistines, like the Israelites, came through the Nile Delta region of Egypt. For further discussion of the origin and migration of the Philistines, see D. M. Howard, “Philistines,” Peoples of the Old Testament World, 232.
The Caphtorites resided in Crete, but in Egyptian literature Caphtor refers to “the region beyond” the Mediterranean.
verses.commentary:
10:14 "Pathrusim" This means southland and probably refers to upper Egypt (BDB 837, KB 991).

▣ "Casluhim (from which came the Philistines)" There has been much discussion about the phrase
in parenthesis because from Jer. 47:4 and Amos 9:7, it seems to imply that the Philistines came from Crete.
This is one of those places where this reference may be geographical. The continuing wave of invasions and
migrations of the sea peoples of the Aegean affected most of the coastlands of the Mediterranean world,
including Egypt and Palestine. For Casluhim see BDB 493, KB 490.

▣ "Caphtorim" This seems to refer to the inhabitants of the island of Crete known as Caphtor
(BDB 499, KB 496). The UBS Text Project, p. 18, suggests that the parenthesis above relates only to "Caphtorim." This
would not be a textual issue but a scribal issue.

verses.zh: 迦南生长子西顿，又生赫
verses.en: Canaan was the father of[NOTE:1] Sidon his firstborn,[NOTE:2] Heth,[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “fathered.”
Sidon was the foremost city in Phoenicia; here Sidon may be the name of its founder.
Some see a reference to “Hittites” here (cf. NIV), but this seems unlikely. See the note on the phrase “sons of Heth” in Gen 23:3.
verses.commentary:
10:15 "Sidon" This is the famous Phoenician seaport and originally its capital, north of Palestine
(BDB 850, KB 1021).

▣ "Heth" This (BDB 366, KB 363) seems to be a non-Semitic name. It is possibly the beginning of the
Hittite group. In the Bible they are located in two places:

- around the city of Hebron

- north of Palestine in central Turkey

They dominated this entire region between 1800-1200 B.C. The tribal group called
Hivites may also be connected to the term Heth.

verses.zh: 和耶布斯人、亚摩利人、革迦撒人、
verses.en: the Jebusites,[NOTE:1] Amorites,[NOTE:2] Girgashites,[NOTE:3]
notes: The Jebusites were the Canaanite inhabitants of ancient Jerusalem.
Here Amorites refers to smaller groups of Canaanite inhabitants of the mountainous regions of Palestine, rather than the large waves of Amurru, or western Semites, who migrated to the region.
The Girgashites are an otherwise unknown Canaanite tribe, though the name is possibly mentioned in Ugaritic texts (see G. J. Wenham, Genesis [WBC], 1:226).
verses.commentary:
10:16 "the Jebusite" These were the occupants of the city of Salem or Jebus, later Jerusalem (BDB 101, KB 382).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MORIAH, SALEM, JEBUS,
JERUSALEM, ZION

▣ "Amorite" The term (BDB 57, KB 67) Amorite can be a collective term (cf. Gen. 15:16) like the term Canaanite. We
think it had the connotation of "high-lander" (the literal name meant "westerner"), while Canaanite had the connotation
of "low-lander" (the literal name meant "land of purple"). In the Bible the inhabitants of Canaan are listed in several places:

- by two tribal groups in Gen. 13:7, 34:30; Jdg. 1:4,5

- by seven nations in Deut. 7:1; Jos. 3:10; 24:11

- by ten nations in Gen. 15:19-21

- the most common usage is a sixth nation designation that is used the majority of times in the Pentateuch

SPECIAL
TOPIC: PRE-ISRAELITE INHABITANTS OF PALESTINE

▣ "Girgashite" This was a Canaanite tribe often named in the various lists of the tribes of Canaan
(BDB 173, KB 202, cf. Gen. 10:16; 15:21; Deut. 7:1; Josh. 3:10; 24:11; Neh. 9:8; 1 Chr. 1:14), but no locality is ever identified.

verses.zh: 希未人、亚基人、西尼人、
verses.en: Hivites,[NOTE:1] Arkites,[NOTE:2] Sinites,[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hivites were Canaanite tribes of a Hurrian origin.
The Arkites lived in Arka, a city in Lebanon, north of Sidon.
The Sinites lived in Sin, another town in Lebanon.
verses.commentary:
10:17 "the Hivite" They seem to be the inhabitants of central Palestine (BDB 295 #2). Some identify them with
Hurrians. Numbers 13:29 is a good geographical summary of the division of these tribes in Palestine.

SPECIAL
TOPIC: PRE-ISRAELITE INHABITANTS OF PALESTINE

▣ "Arkite" This seems to be the inhabitants of a coastal city and island north of Sidon (BDB 792, KB 889).

▣ "Sinite" This seems to be the inhabitants of a city close to Arke (BDB 696, KB 751).

verses.zh: 亚瓦底人、洗玛利人、哈马人，后来迦南的诸族分散了。
verses.en: Arvadites,[NOTE:1] Zemarites,[NOTE:2] and Hamathites.[NOTE:3] Eventually the families of the Canaanites were scattered
notes: The Arvadites lived in the city Arvad, located on an island near the mainland close to the river El Kebir.
The Zemarites lived in the town Sumur, north of Arka.
The Hamathites lived in Hamath on the Orontes River.
verses.commentary:
10:18 "Arvadite" This seems to refer to the inhabitants of an island off the coast north of Palestine
(BDB 71, KB 85). Like the two previous ones it is north of Tripolis.

▣ "Zemarites" This is a Canaanite tribe living on the Mediterranean coast, close to the city
of Arvad (BDB 856, KB 1035). Their main city was called "Sumra" or "Cumur," which later became a large
commercial Phoenician city (Amarna texts).

▣ "Hamathite" This refers to the inhabitants of a city on the Orontes River (BDB 333, KB 331). Verse 18
refers to communities in modern Lebanon.

verses.zh: 迦南的境界是从西顿向基拉耳的路上，直到迦萨，又向所多玛、蛾摩拉、押玛、洗扁的路上，直到拉沙。

notes: Heb “were.”
For location see Map1-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.

verses.commentary:
10:19 "Sodom and Gomorrah and Admah and Zeboiim" These are cities of the plains that God later
destroys. They are located in the southern end of the Dead Sea.

▣ "Lasha" Jerome says that this was east of the Dead Sea (BDB 546, KB 537).

verses.zh: 这就是含的后裔，各随他们的宗族、方言，所住的地土、邦国。
verses.en: These are the sons of Ham, according to their families, according to their languages, by their lands, and by their nations.
verses.commentary: 10:20 This is a summary of the divisions, much like Gen. 10:5.

verses.zh: 雅弗的哥哥闪，是希伯子孙之祖，他也生了儿子。
verses.en: And sons were also born[NOTE:1] to Shem (the older brother of Japheth),[NOTE:2] the father of all the sons of Eber.
notes: Heb “And to Shem was born.”

Or “whose older brother was Japheth.” Some translations render Japheth as the older brother, understanding the adjective הַגָּדוֹל (haggadol, “older”) as modifying Japheth. However, in Hebrew when a masculine singular definite attributive adjective follows the sequence masculine singular construct noun plus proper name, the adjective invariably modifies the noun in construct, not the proper name. Such is the case here. See Deut 11:7; Judg 1:13; 2:7; 3:9; 9:5; 2 Kgs 15:35; 2 Chr 27:3; Neh 3:30; Jer 13:9; 36:10; Ezek 10:19; 11:1.
verses.commentary:
10:21 "Shem" This is the Hebrew term "name" (BDB 1028 II, KB 1551 II). His importance is seen because he is
mentioned both here and in Gen. 11:10-26. The rebellious people of Genesis 10-11 want to build a "name" for
themselves. His name links up with Gen. 4:26 (i.e., YHWH's name glorified). He will represent the chosen
line of blessing (cf. Gen. 12:2).

▣ "Eber" The etymology of this name is very similar to the term "Hebrew" (BDB 720 II, KB 781 II), which
refers to a much wider group than simply the Jews. There has been much speculation about the connection
between Eber and the phrase found on many documents and stele(s) in Egypt called "Habiru" (cf. Gen. 14:13).
A possible etymology of the name Eber is "to pass over and through," which seems to imply a nomadic group.

▣ "the older brother of Japheth" Rashi asserts that the Hebrew is ambiguous as to who is the
older brother.

verses.zh: 闪的儿子是以拦、亚述、亚法撒、路德、亚兰。
verses.en: The sons of Shem were Elam,[NOTE:1] Asshur,[NOTE:2] Arphaxad,[NOTE:3] Lud,[NOTE:4] and Aram.[NOTE:5]
notes: The Hebrew name Elam (עֵילָם, ʿelam) means “highland.” The Elamites were a non-Semitic people who lived east of Babylon.

Asshur is the name for the Assyrians. Asshur was the region in which Nimrod expanded his power (see v. 11, where the name is also mentioned). When names appear in both sections of a genealogical list, it probably means that there were both Hamites and Shemites living in that region in antiquity, especially if the name is a place name.
The descendants of Arphaxad may have lived northeast of Nineveh.
Lud may have been the ancestor of the Ludbu, who lived near the Tigris River.
Aram became the collective name of the northern tribes living in the steppes of Mesopotamia and speaking Aramaic dialects.
verses.commentary:
10:22 "Elam" This was a major kingdom to the east of the Tigris River whose capital was Shushan
(Susa). This is probably the most eastern of the groups mentioned in this chapter (BDB 743, KB 817).

▣ "Asshur" This (BDB 78, KB 94) can refer to

- a person

- a city

- a nation (i.e., Assyria)

- a deity

▣ "Arpachshad" This (BDB 75, KB 90) seems to be a tribal group north of Nineveh (another capital of
Assyria). The NIV translation has Arphaxad.

▣ "Lud" This possibly refers to the Lydian nation of Asia Minor (BDB 530, KB 521-522). Heroditus asserts
that they claimed origin from Nineveh, a Semite city.

▣ "Aram" This refers to the area of modern Syria (BDB 74, KB 89).

verses.zh: 亚兰的儿子是乌斯、户勒、基帖、玛施。
verses.en: The sons of Aram were Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.[NOTE:1]
notes: The MT reads “Mash”; the LXX and 1 Chr 1:17 read “Meshech.”sn Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash. Little is known about these descendants of Aram.

verses.zh: 亚法撒生沙拉；沙拉生希伯。
verses.en: Arphaxad was the father of[NOTE:1] Shelah,[NOTE:2] and Shelah was the father of Eber.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “fathered.”
The MT reads “Arphaxad fathered Shelah”; the LXX reads “Arphaxad fathered Cainan, and Cainan fathered Sala [= Shelah].” The LXX reading also appears to lie behind Luke 3:35-36.
Genesis 11 traces the line of Shem through Eber (עֵבֶר, ʿever) to Abraham the “Hebrew” (עִבְרִי, ʿivri).

verses.zh: 希伯生了两个儿子，一个名叫法勒（就是分的意思），因为那时人就分地居住；法勒的兄弟名叫约坍。
verses.en: Two sons were born to Eber: One was named Peleg because in his days the earth was divided,[NOTE:1] and his brother’s name was Joktan.
notes: The expression “the earth was divided” may refer to dividing the land with canals, but more likely it anticipates the division of languages at Babel (Gen 11). The verb פָּלַג (palag, “separate, divide”) is used in Ps 55:9 for a division of languages.
verses.commentary:
10:25 "Peleg" This is the specific line from which Abraham will come and it is fully discussed
genealogically in Gen. 11:18-27. His name comes from the VERB "divided" (BDB 811 II, KB 929 II).

▣ "for in his days the earth was divided" The Akkadian and Hebrew term "divided," literally means
"irrigation canals," which would fit southern Mesopotamia, but the popular etymology is "divisions" (BDB 811,
KB 928, Niphal PERFECT). There is a sound play between Peleg and divided (niplega). This
may to refer to the dividing of the languages mentioned in chapter 11. Therefore, the dispersions of chapter 10
are out of chronological order when compared to chapter 11.

verses.zh: 约坍生亚摩答、沙列、哈萨玛非、耶拉、
verses.en: Joktan was the father of[NOTE:1] Almodad,[NOTE:2] Sheleph,[NOTE:3] Hazarmaveth,[NOTE:4] Jerah,[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “fathered.”
The name Almodad combines the Arabic article al with modad (“friend”). Almodad was the ancestor of a South Arabian people.
The name Sheleph may be related to Shilph, a district of Yemen; Shalph is a Yemenite tribe.
The name Hazarmaveth should be equated with Hadramawt, located in Southern Arabia.
The name Jerah means “moon.”
verses.commentary: 10:26-29 This is a delineation of the Arabian tribes.

verses.zh: 哈多兰、乌萨、德拉、
verses.en: Hadoram, Uzal,[NOTE:1] Diklah,[NOTE:2]
notes: Uzal was the name of the old capital of Yemen.
The name Diklah means “date-palm.”

verses.zh: 俄巴路、亚比玛利、示巴、
verses.en: Obal,[NOTE:1] Abimael,[NOTE:2] Sheba,[NOTE:3]
notes: Obal was a name used for several localities in Yemen.
The name Abimael is a genuine Sabean form which means “my father, truly, he is God.”
The descendants of Sheba lived in South Arabia, where the Joktanites were more powerful than the Hamites.
verses.commentary:
10:28-29 "Sheba. . .Havilah" This, along with Asshur in Gen. 10:22, seems to be included in both the Hamite
list and the Semite list. This is either because of (1) geographical migration; (2) victories of war; or
(3) the merging of two families by marriage. This list is not specific in many ways.

verses.zh: 阿斐、哈腓拉、约巴，这都是约坍的儿子。
verses.en: Ophir,[NOTE:1] Havilah,[NOTE:2] and Jobab. All these were sons of Joktan.
notes: Ophir became the name of a territory in South Arabia. Many of the references to Ophir are connected with gold (e.g., 1 Kgs 9:28; 10:11; 22:48; 1 Chr 29:4; 2 Chr 8:18; 9:10; Job 22:24; 28:16; Ps 45:9; Isa 13:12).
Havilah is listed with Ham in v. 7.

verses.en: Their dwelling place was from Mesha all the way to[NOTE:1] Sephar in the eastern hills.

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

INTRODUCTION

- What is the theological purpose of the detailed nature of Genesis 10?

- It shows that God is concerned with all nations. Genesis 11 is chronologically out of
order. This seems to show that Genesis 10 is not only a judgment (cf. Gen. 11:1-9), but
primarily the fulfillment of Gen. 1:28 and 9:1,7 (i.e., be fruitful and fill the earth).

- These same nations are often referred to in the Prophets (cf. Isa. 7-23; Jer. 46-51;
Ezek. 27-30; 38-39) as groups that God later judges.

- It sets the stage for the call of Abraham and his seed as a kingdom of priests to bring
all the world (i.e., the surrounding nations) to YHWH (cf. Gen. 12:3; Exod. 19:5-6).
SPECIAL
TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

- It follows the pattern of Genesis of the narrowing focus of the Messianic line
(cf. Gen. 9:26).

- There seem to be about 70 groups mentioned. Later Rabbinical Midrash says that there
are 70 languages of the known world, possibly from LXX of Deut. 32:8. Many link Luke 10:1
with this to assert the worldwide missionary thrust of the Gospel (i.e., Jesus sends out
the disciples).

- How and why does it disagree with modern ethnological research?

- Modern research is based on linguistic principles while the biblical account
focuses on geographical data. This geographical information is affected by

- date

- people movements both from migration and war (cf. Ezek. 16:3)

- One must take into account the theological nature of this account

- Selective coverage

- Unity of mankind (Adam and Noah)

- Those nations farthest from contact with Israel are dealt with least
(or not at all)

- This chapter contains many PLURAL names. This shows that often an
ancestor stands for a group. Often, groups occupy more than one geographical location.

- This is not a western, detailed, scientific account. We often forget that this is the
first attempt at a list of this type. Its accuracy is assured by our pre-suppositional
commitment to Scripture. However, this does not mean it was meant to inform us exhaustively
in all areas or conform to our western mind-set. For its day it is shockingly accurate!

- This list, as all of the Torah, was subject to scribal revisions and updating. Several
of the names in this list

- Cimmerians

- Scythians

- Philistines

- Medes

are not found in other Ancient Near Eastern literature until 1500-1000 B.C.

- It is possible because the peoples of Asia and Polynesia (and therefy the Americas) and many
of the peoples of Africa are not dealt with, that this list may include only part of the racial diversity
observable today. If this is true then it is a theological overstatement to say the races came directly
from Noah's three children.

This is not meant to diminish the oneness of humans (which DNA studies have confirmed),
which is clearly asserted in the original human pair.

- Its structure (i.e., the nations that surround and interact with Israel)

- Japheth, Gen. 10:2-5, occupies the region north of Mesopotamia from Spain to the
Caspian Sea.

- Ham, Gen. 10:6-20, occupies the region south of Mesopotamia from Africa to India

- Shem, Gen. 10:21ff, deals with the Semites' occupation of Mesopotamia from the
Mediterranean Sea to India.
